examples.solution_text:
Multiply the coefficient by the power, then reduce the power by $1$.
$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=-\dfrac{2}{5}\cdot5x^{5-1}\\&=-2x^4\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Differentiate $f(x)=4x^{-7}$ with respect to $x$. Leave your answer in index notation.
Differentiate $f(x)=-\dfrac{9}{4x^3}$ with respect to $x$. Express your answer as a single fraction with a positive index.
examples.solution_text:
Rewrite using a negative index.
$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=-\dfrac{9}{4}x^{-3}\end{aligned}$
Apply the power rule, then rewrite as a fraction.
$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=-\dfrac{9}{4}(-3)x^{-4}\\&=\dfrac{27}{4}x^{-4}\\&=\dfrac{27}{4x^4}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Differentiate $f(x)=5x^{\frac{2}{3}}$ with respect to $x$, for $x>0$. Leave your answer in index notation.

Differentiate each function with respect to $x$. Express your answers in surd form.
a. $f(x)=10\sqrt{x}$, where $x>0$.
b. $g(x)=\dfrac{6}{\sqrt[3]{x}}$, where $x\ne0$.
examples.solution_text:
a. Rewrite the square root using a fractional index.
$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=10x^{\frac{1}{2}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=10\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}x^{\frac{1}{2}-1}\\&=5x^{-\frac{1}{2}}\\&=\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{x}}\end{aligned}$
b. Rewrite the reciprocal cube root using a negative fractional index.
$\begin{aligned}g(x)&=6x^{-\frac{1}{3}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}g'(x)&=6\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)x^{-\frac{1}{3}-1}\\&=-2x^{-\frac{4}{3}}\\&=-\dfrac{2}{\sqrt[3]{x^4}}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Rewrite each function as a single power of $x$, then differentiate. Express your answers in surd form. Assume $x>0$.
a. $f(x)=3x^3\sqrt{x}$.
b. $g(x)=\dfrac{4x^2}{\sqrt{x^3}}$.
c. $h(x)=\dfrac{2}{5x\sqrt{x}}$.
examples.solution_text:
a. Add the indices when multiplying powers of $x$.
$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=3x^3x^{\frac{1}{2}}\\&=3x^{\frac{7}{2}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=3\cdot\dfrac{7}{2}x^{\frac{5}{2}}\\&=\dfrac{21}{2}x^2\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}$
b. Subtract the denominator's index from the numerator's index.
$\begin{aligned}g(x)&=\dfrac{4x^2}{x^{\frac{3}{2}}}\\&=4x^{\frac{1}{2}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}g'(x)&=4\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}x^{-\frac{1}{2}}\\&=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}}\end{aligned}$
c. Combine the powers in the denominator before rewriting.
$\begin{aligned}h(x)&=\dfrac{2}{5x^{\frac{3}{2}}}\\&=\dfrac{2}{5}x^{-\frac{3}{2}}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}h'(x)&=\dfrac{2}{5}\left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)x^{-\frac{5}{2}}\\&=-\dfrac{3}{5x^2\sqrt{x}}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Differentiate each function with respect to $x$, where $a$, $r$, $b$, $k$ and $p$ are constants. Assume $x>0$.
a. $f(x)=ax^r$.
b. $g(x)=bx^{2k+3}$.
c. $h(x)=\dfrac{p}{x^{3r}}$, where $r>0$. Express this answer as a fraction with a positive index.
examples.solution_text:
a. Treat $a$ and $r$ as constants. For $r\ne0$,
$f'(x)=arx^{r-1}$.
If $r=0$, the function is constant and $f'(x)=0$.
b. Use the complete exponent $2k+3$ as the multiplier.
$\begin{aligned}g'(x)&=b(2k+3)x^{(2k+3)-1}\\&=b(2k+3)x^{2k+2}\end{aligned}$
If $k=-\dfrac{3}{2}$, the function is constant and $g'(x)=0$.
c. Rewrite the denominator using a negative index.
$h(x)=px^{-3r}$.
$\begin{aligned}h'(x)&=p(-3r)x^{-3r-1}\\&=-\dfrac{3rp}{x^{3r+1}}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Find each derivative value.
a. $f'(2)$, given $f(x)=3x^4$.
b. $g'(9)$, given $g(x)=12\sqrt{x}$.
c. $h'(27)$, given $h(x)=x^{\frac{4}{3}}$.
examples.solution_text:
Differentiate first, then substitute the given input into the derivative.
a. $f'(x)=12x^3$.
$\begin{aligned}f'(2)&=12(2)^3\\&=96\end{aligned}$
b. $g(x)=12x^{\frac{1}{2}}$, so $g'(x)=6x^{-\frac{1}{2}}=\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{x}}$.
$\begin{aligned}g'(9)&=\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{9}}\\&=2\end{aligned}$
c. $h'(x)=\dfrac{4}{3}x^{\frac{1}{3}}$.
$\begin{aligned}h'(27)&=\dfrac{4}{3}\sqrt[3]{27}\\&=4\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: Applying the coefficient and power rules gives (-2/5)(5)x^(5-1) = -2x^4.
Rewrite as (-9/4)x^(-3). Differentiation gives (27/4)x^(-4) = 27/(4x^4), for x nonzero.
Multiply 5 by 2/3 and subtract 1 from 2/3, obtaining (10/3)x^(-1/3) on x>0.
For a, 10x^(1/2) differentiates to 5x^(-1/2) = 5/sqrt(x). For b, 6x^(-1/3) differentiates to -2x^(-4/3) = -2/cuberoot(x^4), valid for either sign of nonzero x.
On x>0: a becomes 3x^(7/2), giving (21/2)x^2 sqrt(x); b becomes 4x^(1/2), giving 2/sqrt(x); c becomes (2/5)x^(-3/2), giving -3/(5x^2 sqrt(x)).

For a, the derivative is arx^(r-1), with derivative zero when r=0. For b, the complete exponent gives b(2k+3)x^(2k+2), with derivative zero when k=-3/2. For c, px^(-3r) gives -3rp/x^(3r+1); r>0 ensures a positive denominator index.
